prompt: In what year did the RMS Titanic sink?
fact: She hit the iceberg late on 14 April and was gone by 2:20 a.m. on the 15th. More than 1,500 people died.

prompt: How many lifeboats did the Titanic carry?
fact: Room for about 1,178 people, roughly half of those aboard. It was still more than the law required.

prompt: Which ship raced through the ice to pick up the Titanic's survivors?
fact: The Californian was close enough to see Titanic's distress rockets, and did nothing.

prompt: What was the name of the Titanic's bandleader, who kept playing as the ship went down?
fact: His violin was recovered and sold at auction in 2013 for about £900,000 before fees.

prompt: Roughly how deep does the Titanic wreck lie?
fact: About 3,800 metres down. Robert Ballard and Jean-Louis Michel found it in 1985.

prompt: Which international rulebook was written because the Titanic sank?
fact: The first SOLAS convention, in 1914, required lifeboat space for everyone aboard and a 24-hour radio watch.

prompt: Which of Titanic's sister ships sank in 1916 after hitting a mine while serving as a hospital ship?
fact: Stewardess Violet Jessop survived both the Titanic and the Britannic.

prompt: The SS Edmund Fitzgerald went down in November 1975 on which Great Lake?
fact: All 29 crew were lost. Gordon Lightfoot's 1976 song made her the most famous Great Lakes wreck.

prompt: What was the Edmund Fitzgerald carrying when she sank?
fact: About 26,000 tons of taconite pellets, bound for Detroit.

prompt: In 1915 the SS Eastland rolled onto her side while still tied up at the dock. In which city?
fact: 844 people died in the Chicago River, most of them employees heading to a company picnic.

prompt: A German U-boat sank the RMS Lusitania in 1915 off the coast of which country?
fact: 1,198 people died, 128 of them American, which helped turn US opinion against Germany.

prompt: Just before she was torpedoed in 1945, the USS Indianapolis delivered parts for what?
choices: The first atomic bomb used in war
fact: Of about 1,195 men aboard, only 316 survived days in the water. Quint tells the story in Jaws.

prompt: The Wilhelm Gustloff, sunk in 1945, is the deadliest single ship sinking ever. Who was mostly aboard?
choices: Civilians fleeing the advancing Soviet army
Navy cadets on a training cruise
fact: Estimates of the dead run past 9,000, several times the Titanic's toll.

prompt: The submarine Kursk sank in the Barents Sea in 2000. Which navy did she belong to?
fact: A faulty torpedo exploded during an exercise. All 118 crew died.

prompt: In 1917 a munitions ship collided with another vessel and caused the biggest man-made explosion before the atomic bomb. Which harbour?
fact: The SS Mont-Blanc blew up after colliding with the SS Imo. About 2,000 people were killed.

prompt: The Swedish warship Vasa capsized on her maiden voyage in 1628. How far did she get?
fact: She sank about 1,300 metres out. Raised in 1961, she is now a museum in Stockholm and around 98% original.

prompt: The Mary Rose sank in 1545 in front of the very king whose flagship she was. Which king?
fact: She was raised from the Solent in 1982, watched live on TV by an estimated 60 million people.

prompt: The 1852 wreck of HMS Birkenhead is credited with starting which rule?
choices: Captain goes down with the ship
fact: The soldiers aboard stood in ranks on deck so the women and children could reach the boats.

prompt: After the 1789 mutiny on the Bounty, where did the mutineers hide from the Royal Navy?
fact: They burned the Bounty there. Their descendants still live on Pitcairn today.

prompt: Set adrift by the mutineers, Captain Bligh sailed an open boat about 3,600 nautical miles. Where did he land?
fact: It took 47 days with 18 men in a 23-foot launch. Bligh lost only one of them on the voyage.

prompt: The Dutch ship Batavia wrecked in 1629 and a mutineer took over the survivors' islands. Off which coast?
fact: Jeronimus Cornelisz and his followers murdered more than 100 survivors before rescue arrived.

prompt: What sank the whaleship Essex in the Pacific in 1820?
fact: The whale rammed the ship twice. The story inspired Herman Melville's Moby-Dick.

prompt: The Mary Celeste was found drifting in 1872 with no one aboard. In which ocean?
fact: Her cargo was intact and one lifeboat was gone. The ten people aboard were never found.

prompt: Franklin's lost 1845 Arctic expedition sailed in HMS Erebus and HMS what?
fact: All 129 men died. The wrecks were finally found in 2014 and 2016.

prompt: Shackleton's Endurance was crushed by pack ice in 1915. In which sea?
fact: All 28 men survived. The wreck was found in 2022, about 3,000 metres down and remarkably intact.

prompt: In 1956 the Italian liner Andrea Doria sank off Nantucket after colliding with which ship?
fact: Rescuers took off more than 1,600 people. The Île de France turned back to help and saved over 750.

prompt: The Empress of Ireland sank in 1914 in just 14 minutes. On which river?
fact: 1,012 died. More passengers were lost than on the Titanic, though fewer crew.

prompt: The cruise ship Costa Concordia ran aground in 2012 off which Italian island?
fact: Captain Francesco Schettino left the ship before everyone was off. He was sentenced to 16 years.

prompt: The ferry MS Estonia sank in 1994 when her bow door tore off in a storm. In which sea?
fact: 852 people died, making it one of the deadliest peacetime sinkings in Europe.

prompt: The steamboat Sultana, the worst maritime disaster in US history, exploded in 1865 on which river?
fact: Most of the roughly 1,100 dead were Union soldiers just released from Confederate prison camps.

prompt: The SS Central America, lost in a hurricane in 1857, was carrying tons of what?
choices: Gold from the California Gold Rush
fact: The lost gold helped set off the Panic of 1857. The wreck is nicknamed the Ship of Gold.

prompt: The Exxon Valdez spilled millions of gallons of oil in 1989 off which US state?
fact: It ran aground on Bligh Reef in Prince William Sound, named for the same William Bligh of the Bounty.

prompt: After the tanker Torrey Canyon ran aground off Cornwall in 1967, what did the British government do?
fact: RAF jets dropped bombs and napalm to burn off the oil. A good share of the bombs missed.
